evidence: The authoritative workbook Quality Checks!D2 asks whether the prompt reads like a real person requesting an app; Internal Quality Checks!D2 repeats that wording without an additional annotation. The frozen instruction.md:1 opens, 'I'd like a small local playground for working on JavaScript and complete HTML files,' then describes a first-person workflow: pasting a long line, formatting, editing in several places, running beside the source, and keeping versions despite another tab saving first. Lines 3 and 5 ask the builder to read six linked notes and put the app in /app, but the prompt contains no numbered acceptance list, feature matrix, framework mandate, endpoint list, or build recipe. Those two short delivery directions do not displace the natural product ask. The detailed notes are linked requirements, rather than checklist prose pasted into the primary prompt. A static mock could still pass this style-only row while failing product-function rows; conversely, a working app requested through a numbered specification could fail this row. This row is settled by source inspection, so no runtime measurement is needed.
